name: Pfalz

communes: Ilbesheim Bei Landau In Der Pfalz

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Riesling, Müller-Thurgau, Spätburgunder and Grauburgunder sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: Qualitätswein
German quality wine from one of the specified regions. It can be dry to sweet.
Prädikatswein
Germany's top tier, graded by how ripe the grapes are at harvest. Unless the label says dry or off-dry, expect some sweetness.
Kabinett
Light wine from fully ripe grapes of the main harvest, often semi-sweet with crisp acidity.
Spätlese
Late harvest. Often sweeter and fruitier than Kabinett.
Auslese
Select harvest from fully ripe or noble-rotted grapes.
Beerenauslese (BA)
Overripe berries picked one by one, often with noble rot. Rich, sweet dessert wine.
Trockenbeerenauslese (TBA)
Overripe berries shriveled on the vine, often with noble rot. Extremely rich and sweet. Trocken here means dried grapes, not a dry wine.
Eiswein
Ice wine, from grapes frozen naturally on the vine. The must is at least as sweet as a Beerenauslese.
Trocken, Halbtrocken
Dry and medium dry. Under EU rules a dry wine has no more than 4 g of sugar a liter, or a little more when its acidity is high. Medium dry has more sugar than that.
VDP, Grosses Gewächs (GG)
The VDP is an association of about 200 estates with rules stricter than the law. GG is its top dry wine from its best sites.
keyfacts: It has many hours of sunshine and lies between the forested Haardt Mountains and the Rhine plain.
The region has two districts, Südliche Weinstraße in the south and Mittelhaardt-Deutsche Weinstraße in the north.
White grapes cover 69% of the vineyard and red grapes 31%, and most of the red wine is made dry.

notes: Pfalz wines are traditionally dry and full bodied.
Riesling here can develop citrus and peach notes, and its Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris are among Germany's most powerful.

blurb.text: Germany's second-largest wine region, with about ⟦area|58,560 acres|23,700 hectares⟧ under vine in 2022. Known as Rheinpfalz before 1993. Riesling leads the plantings at 24%, followed by the red Dornfelder at 14%, with Müller-Thurgau and Spätburgunder behind.
